_what: ⛔ SNG-642 §4 (C16) — NINE ARTIFACTS THAT WORK, AND FEED, plus the Unmet's. ✅ Erik: "If a PC finds one (or NPC) they can use it… but it would likely be helping feed the sovereign." ⛑ EVERY USE IS A DEED TOWARD THE SOVEREIGN'S ARC, whoever uses it. R40b.4: agents push as ordinary figures, and nothing marks the user as an agent — using one makes you part of the supply line without knowing it, which is the lore's "individually reasonable, cumulatively impossible" with the player's own hand on it.
_marks: ⚡ Each artifact IS one of SNG-641's marks: holding it counts as having seen that mark, so a player who learned the lidless ring recognises the Lidless Ring.
_forbidTags: ⚠️ `forbidTags` IS CCODE'S, NOT AEVI'S. §5 asks for the cost to be ENFORCED and the staged data carries `whatItCosts` as prose; a reader cannot enforce a sentence. Only the two she named carry one, and each value comes out of her own cost sentence — see `_forbidTagsWhy`. The other seven costs are narrative or are about somebody else, and reach the GM as prose.

items.name: the Lidless Ring
items.description: A heavy gold ring worked as a circle of rays around an empty centre. It is warm, and it is always slightly brighter than the room.
items.whatItDoes: Nothing within arm's reach can be hidden from the wearer — a lie shows, a concealed thing is noticed, a false face slips.
items.whatItCosts: The wearer cannot hide either: no stealth, no disguise, no secret kept while it is on. It does not want to come off.

feeds.perUse: one deed toward the arc, entered as the user's push — NPC or PC, R40b.4

items.name: the Open Lantern
items.description: A brass lantern with no shutter and no door. The flame inside was never lit and cannot be put out.
items.whatItDoes: Its light shows what is concealed: hidden doors, veiled craft, what the Umbral keep.
items.whatItCosts: It cannot be dimmed. Whoever carries it is seen by everything, from very far away.

items.name: the Herald's Brand
items.description: A branding iron with the lidless ring at its end. It heats without a fire.
items.whatItDoes: Whatever it brands is believed: a filing, a crate, a claim, a person's word.
items.whatItCosts: Anything branded can never again be private. The board clerks who use it confess in their sleep.

feeds.perUse: one deed toward the arc, entered as the user's push — NPC or PC, R40b.4

items.name: the Hollow Coin
items.description: A coin with its face worn smooth on purpose. It passes at full weight anywhere, and it always comes back.
items.whatItDoes: Spent on any petition, the answer is yes.
items.whatItCosts: A notch is cut in your door frame for every yes, and the coin always finds its way back to your purse, so you can ask again.

feeds.perUse: one deed toward the arc, entered as the user's push — NPC or PC, R40b.4

items.name: the Seam Contract
items.description: A blank contract on heavy paper, with one ruled line below where the signatures go.
items.whatItDoes: Whatever two parties write on it is kept, by both, absolutely.
items.whatItCosts: The blank line below the signatures is filled in later, by someone who was not in the room.

feeds.perUse: one deed toward the arc, entered as the user's push — NPC or PC, R40b.4

items.name: the Seal of Leave
items.description: A signet with nothing cut into its face. The wax it leaves carries a mark anyway, and nobody can quite describe it.
items.whatItDoes: A claim sealed with it reads as granted — lawful, recognised, beyond argument — to anyone who sees the wax.
items.whatItCosts: It makes the claim legitimate by grant, not by credibility, and the Mavens can tell the difference. An empty chair appears at the holder's table.

feeds.perUse: one deed toward the arc, entered as the user's push — NPC or PC, R40b.4

items._foundAt: carried by the Bright Bargain's envoy (power_gralloch_crown)

items.name: the Ninefold Chit
items.description: A nine-sided Cogitarium token of a pale stone that is not quite stone. It is always cool.
items.whatItDoes: Held while you sleep, it lets the mind work on while the body rests: you wake with the answer.
items.whatItCosts: Each use you sleep a little longer and wake a little further away. Your eyes move under the lids.

feeds.perUse: one deed toward the arc, entered as the user's push — NPC or PC, R40b.4

items.name: the Choirmaster's Fork
items.description: A tuning fork of dark metal. Struck, it gives no sound you can hear; sleepers nearby hum four bars.
items.whatItDoes: Through any sleeper who hums, you can hear what they are near.
items.whatItCosts: Every sleeper you listen through sleeps deeper. Some of them stop waking.

feeds.perUse: one deed toward the arc, entered as the user's push — NPC or PC, R40b.4

items._foundAt: the Thinning, where the Choirmaster keeps his choir (the_thinning)

items.name: the Cold Seal
items.description: A Dusklow crate seal stamped cold goods — do not open. It frosts whatever it closes.
items.whatItDoes: Whatever is sealed with it is kept exactly as it was: food, medicine, a wound — a living body, which does not age.
items.whatItCosts: Nobody sealed with it has ever been let out by the person who sealed them.

feeds.perUse: one deed toward the arc, entered as the user's push — NPC or PC, R40b.4

items.name: the Farlong Map
items.description: A traveller's map that redraws itself in pale ink. There is one road on it that runs off the edge.
items.whatItDoes: It always shows a shorter way. You are never lost and never caught.
items.whatItCosts: The destination drifts. You never quite arrive, and the people waiting for you begin to forget your face.

feeds.perUse: one deed toward the arc, entered as the user's push — NPC or PC, R40b.4

items.name: the Parting Glass
items.description: A plain travelling cup of horn, rimmed in worn silver. Two people who drink from it part without grief.
items.whatItDoes: Any parting made over it is clean: no grudge, no pursuit, no grief. A feud ends; a hunter lets you go.
items.whatItCosts: You never meet again, whatever either of you does. The distance is kept.
